morning.caption:
$79.57. That was WTI early Tuesday, the lowest since late August, after crude lost 4.5% on Monday as Washington signaled more time for Iran diplomacy and inventory data pointed to a surplus.

Producers budgeting for 2027 feel it first. Refiners get cheaper crude, but fuel futures fell almost as fast.

midday.caption:
TotalEnergies is buying more American gas. A new deal with Continental Resources should add about 150 MMcf/d of net production by 2032, though neither the price nor the basin was disclosed.

The largest US LNG exporter of 2025 now owns more of the molecules it ships abroad.

evening.caption:
Egypt wants its Nargis gas sooner. Petroleum Minister Karim Badawi met Chevron and Eni on Saturday to push the offshore field forward after the Nargis-2 well found up to 35 metres of net pay.

There is still no cost, schedule or start date.
